page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance designed for high-density compute and memory workloads. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 192 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors operating at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. With a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, each vCPU maps to a dedicated physical core. System memory consists of 1536 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, resulting in 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The hardware profile includes AVX-512 vector extensions, AES and VAES cryptographic acceleration, and 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage drives.

In empirical benchmarks, the r7a.48xlarge demonstrates high throughput across multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The instance achieved a multi-core CPU stress-ng score of 588,964.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 143,337.26, both placing in the top ten percent of tested cloud servers. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 652.3 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show top-tier execution in database and web serving environments, recording 323.08 million Redis SET operations per second and 109.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Software compilation via Geekbench Clang attained a score of 70,654. LLM prompt processing speed reached 4,194.28 tokens per second on a 135M model and 351.24 tokens per second on a 7B model.

Tradeoffs include the absence of onboard local storage, necessitating network-attached storage options such as EBS for persistent data holding. Additionally, while prompt processing is fast, LLM text generation rates remain constrained compared to dedicated GPU systems, yielding 64.02 tokens per second on small models. From a cost efficiency perspective, the provision of 192 dedicated physical cores alongside 1.5 TB of high-bandwidth DDR5 memory consolidates heavy enterprise tasks onto a single instance, reducing multi-node synchronization overhead. The r7a.48xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource management systems, software compilation clusters, and heavy ETL data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture and powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9R14 processor cores running at 3.7 GHz and 1536 GB of DDR5 RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio with 652.3 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. The instance provides 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes AVX-512 instruction set extensions. Benchmark results highlight top-tier performance in multi-core processing, static web serving throughput, software compilation, and in-memory key-value operations such as Redis SET performance reaching 323 million operations per second. However, it lacks attached local storage, relying on external network storage, and exhibits lower token generation rates during CPU-based LLM inference compared to GPU-accelerated architectures. The high memory density and dedicated core allocation provide qualitative cost efficiency for resource-demanding enterprise applications, large-scale in-memory databases, and compute-intensive compilation workloads.
